- Question b, fact: A real place, Port Fairy, is named with a model giving a 4 m tidal range (depth 4 m to 8 m). Port Fairy's actual tidal range is about a metre, so the setting implies an unrealistic tide. A generic jetty, or a smaller amplitude, would avoid this. Minor.

rejected.title: Modelling with sine and cosine
card: Things that rise and fall in a regular cycle, such as tides, daylight hours and temperatures, can be modelled by y = a sin(nx) + k or y = a cos(nx) + k.
Mean
The mean k is the middle value of the cycle. It is halfway between the greatest and least values, so k = (greatest + least) ÷ 2.
Amplitude
The amplitude a is how far the value rises above the mean. It is half the gap between greatest and least, so a = (greatest − least) ÷ 2.
Period
The period is the time for one full cycle, and it equals 2π ÷ n. Example: a tide with high 5 m, low 1 m and a 12 hour cycle has mean 3 m, amplitude 2 m and n = 2π ÷ 12 = π/6.
rejected.remember: Mean is halfway between the extremes, amplitude is half the gap, period is one cycle.

a.q: The temperature in a cool room cycles between 14°C and 22°C. What is the amplitude of a sine model for it?
a.why: The amplitude is half the gap: (22 − 14) ÷ 2 = 4. The option 8°C is the whole gap from least to greatest, not the distance from the middle.
a.clue: Amplitude is measured from the middle line, not from bottom to top.

b.q: Water depth at a Port Fairy jetty is modelled by d = 2 sin(nt) + 6, in metres, with t in hours. One full tide cycle takes 12 hours. What is n?
b.why: The period is 2π ÷ n = 12, so n = 2π ÷ 12 = π/6. Check: 2π ÷ (π/6) = 12. The option 6/π comes from dividing 12 by 2π, which turns the division upside down.
b.clue: Put the period into period = 2π ÷ n and solve for n.

final.title: Modelling with sine and cosine
card: Things that rise and fall in a regular cycle, such as tides, daylight hours and temperatures, can be modelled by \(y = a \sin(nx) + k\) or \(y = a \cos(nx) + k\).
Mean
The mean \(k\) is the middle value of the cycle. It is halfway between the greatest and least values, so \(k = (\text{greatest} + \text{least}) \div 2\).
Amplitude
The amplitude \(a\) is how far the value rises above the mean. It is half the gap between greatest and least, so \(a = (\text{greatest} - \text{least}) \div 2\).
Period

The period is the time for one full cycle, and it equals \(2\pi \div n\). Example: a tide with high 5 m, low 1 m and a 12 hour cycle has mean 3 m, amplitude 2 m and \(n = 2\pi \div 12 = \frac{\pi}{6}\).
final.remember: Mean is halfway between the extremes, amplitude is half the gap, period is one cycle.

a.q: The temperature in a cool room cycles between 14°C and 22°C. What is the amplitude of a sine model for it?
a.why: The amplitude is half the gap: \((22 - 14) \div 2 = 4\). The option 8°C is the whole gap from least to greatest, not the distance from the middle.
a.clue: Amplitude is measured from the middle line, not from bottom to top.

b.q: Water depth at a small harbour jetty is modelled by \(d = 0.5 \sin(nt) + 2\), in metres, with \(t\) in hours. One full tide cycle takes 12 hours. What is \(n\)?
b.why: The period is \(2\pi \div n = 12\), so \(n = 2\pi \div 12 = \frac{\pi}{6}\). Check: \(2\pi \div \frac{\pi}{6} = 12\). The option \(\frac{6}{\pi}\) comes from dividing 12 by \(2\pi\), which turns the division upside down.
b.clue: Put the period into \(\text{period} = 2\pi \div n\) and solve for \(n\).
